newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha at four-year high on bullish crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha at four-year high on bullish crudes.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha reached its highest level in four years in Tuesday afternoon trade, buoyed by bullish overnight crude markets, traders said.
However, trading was subdued with most sellers on the sidelines awaiting further naphtha gains, they added.
First-half December open-spec naphtha was quoted at $215.00/$216.00. It was traded at $212.50 in late trading on Monday.
Second-half December was assessed at $214.50/$215.50, up from Monday's $211.25/$212.25.
Open-spec naphtha cargoes have mostly been quoted below the $200.00 level after having reached around $217.00 in June 1992, traders said.
Naphtha spreads were virtually unchanged, with first-half December/first-half January talked at plus 75 cents/$1.50.
Potential kerosene importers remained relaxed amid ample spot offers in the market, middle distillate traders said.
Rumours of Middle Eastern cargoes sold into China at a discount after having failed to find buyers in the Japanese market further weakened sentiment, they said.
